chapter: New Orleans bands, Louis and the Lyric
title: Zutty the gentleman: finer things, horse shows
summary: Marge says musicians are wrongly pictured as drunkards; Zutty was neat and gentlemanly and took her to Madison Square Garden horse shows.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: But it didn't mean anything to Zutty because that was his life. He liked it. As I say, he liked the finer things in life, you see people always pick..... That's why I tell a lot because you always picture musicians as being drunkards. And you make them drunk because if they don't want to drink you insist on them having a drink. But they are fine men, a whole lot of them. Now Zutty, that's what I tell

them, you know old Zutty (opens up his big mouth?) and says when I met you you didn't (speak over a whisper?) and associating with those low musicians you've gotten just like them. (LAUGHTER). Because I must say without an education or anything, Zutty was such a gentleman. That's what I liked about him. As a musician and so neat, so clean. And liked the finer things. So many things he's made me go to that I don't care a thing about. Like here in New York, the horse shows at the Madison Square Garden. All those kind of things that show they come from.....
The Russian show and that show that came from those, with those fine horses in them, Austria....
Yes, he asked me to go see that. I say, I don't care about...... Well I want to see it. 'I want to see it and you will enjoy it.'
He always liked the beautiful things.
That sort of thing makes you broad minded you know.
